incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty ALERT - PAGER FIRED for inference-hosting-prod (us-west-2)
Trigger: p99 latency > 3.0s for 10m (current p99=3.62s)
Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345

alice.m (oncall): Ack, I'm on it. Investigating tail latency.

bob.sre: Looking at autoscaler and runtime metrics now. Seeing multiple failed scale attempts 10m ago with API quota 429s to cloud provider. Could be partial capacity loss.

carol_runtime: p95 stayed ~600ms but p99 spike to 3.6s. KV-cache miss rate spiked at same time (see below). Could be cache eviction cascade.

alice.m (oncall): dave_support can you confirm customer-facing errors? Any SLO pages from customers?

dave_support: Yes — two customers reported timeouts in chat widgets starting ~1755504200. Errors are 504 gateway-timeout in edge logs. Support ticket IDs: #CS-8241, #CS-8242. Impact: small percentage of realtime requests are timing out, mainly low-latency SLAs.

erin_prodops: Adding note: there was a backend deploy 12m ago that adjusted continuous-batching policy (max_batch_ms lowered to 8ms -> 2ms) and enabled dynamic batching thresholds. Could be related.

bob.sre: grabbing pod logs for runtime shard a3-7:```
kubectl -n inference logs inference-runtime-a3-7 | tail -n 120
# repeated warnings: "failed to allocate kv cache slot" / "batching negotiation timed out"
# 429 from cloud provider for node create: quotaExceeded
```

carol_runtime: Also seeing GC pause spikes on a few pods around 1755504180 - 1755504220. Combined with failed scale attempts, tail requests queued and hit long GC/queueing.

alice.m (oncall): Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) disable continuous batching on affected pool, 2) route 25% of traffic to fallback-model-small (lower latency), 3) scale down batch size. I'll run 1 and 2 now.

bob.sre: Can we do a graceful reroute via routing policy? If we flip 25% to fallback it should reduce pressure. I can run the route change.

alice.m (oncall): rolling change:```
# disable continuous batching for pool inference-a3
redwoodctl config set pool/inference-a3/continuous_batching false --dry-run
redwoodctl config set pool/inference-a3/continuous_batching false --apply
# route 25% to fallback model
redwoodctl routing set-weight inference-hosting-prod fallback-model-small 25
```

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty note: Incident acknowledged by alice.m at 1755504330. Escalation to SRE lead in 10m if not resolved.

bob.sre: Applied routing change and disabled continuous batching. Observing immediate reduction in queue depth on nodes. p99 trending down from 3.6s -> 1.8s now.

carol_runtime: Confirmed fallback-model-small p99 ~450ms. Main pool p99 improved to ~1.2s within 60s. KV cache eviction rate down 70%. GC pauses still present on older pods; consider recycle.

erin_prodops: I'm requesting a hot-restart of the three pods with highest GC time to recover memory fragmentation:```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime-a3 --selector=gc_high=true
```

alice.m (oncall): Good. Noted customer impact and actions for postmortem: recent batching config change + quota issue during autoscale + memory fragmentation caused tail. Taking notes.

dave_support: Notifying affected customer contacts that we've applied mitigation and are seeing reduced errors. Will escalate billing/credits if SLA breach confirmed.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty update: Escalation suppressed at 1755504395 (ack still active).

bob.sre: After restarts p99 down to 560ms on main pool, overall p99 ~420ms. Autoscaler calls now succeeding. Cloud quota errors drop to zero. Looks stable.

alice.m (oncall): Reverting 25% route after stabilization? We should keep fallback at 10% for safety and gradually move back. Also plan: revert the recent batching policy change and open a change with load-tests.

carol_runtime: Agreed. I'm opening PR to revert aggressive batching policy and add a canary gating step. Link: https://git.example/repo/pulls/789

erin_prodops: I'll create a quota increase request with cloud and schedule follow-up on autoscaler error handling.

alice.m (oncall): Handoff note for next oncall: initial cause likely config change + transient cloud quota. Mitigations performed: disabled continuous batching, routed 25% then scaled back to 10% fallback-model-small, restarted high-GC pods. Current status: p99=420ms, errors returned to baseline.

incident-bot: SUMMARY (automated): Incident INC12345 - SLO p99 latency burn - acknowledged 1755504330, mitigations applied 1755504345-1755504410, stabilized 1755504475. Postmortem owner: carol_runtime.

alice.m (oncall): Handoff complete. If anything regresses ping me and I'll re-open. :thumbsup:

erin_prodops: Marking incident as mitigated but not closed. Will coordinate postmortem and quota request.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident resolved at 1755504587 (no further paging).
